meta.scope: Guyana batch 1 — Phase 0+1. Core national statistical system, oil-driven transformation, Natural Resource Fund, census, and labour. Definition locked. Guyana is the fastest-growing economy in the region on the back of offshore oil.
meta.strategy_note: Follows NEXT-COUNTRY-STRATEGY.md after Venezuela checkpoint. Small population (~0.9–1.0 m), extreme oil-driven GDP growth, Natural Resource Fund as the central fiscal institution.

candidates.title: Bureau of Statistics (BoS) — institutional statistical identity
candidates.description: National statistical office. Produces census, labour-force, national-accounts and other official statistics.
referenced_by: Budget and planning documents that cite BoS series
candidates.notes: Institutional parent node for Guyanese official statistics. Semi-autonomous body under the Minister of Finance.

candidates.title: Population and Housing Census
candidates.description: Decennial population and housing census. 2022 census recorded 878,674 persons (up 17.6% from 2012), reversing prior decline; projections approach ~950k+ by mid-decade.
candidates.notes: Foundational demographic product. Documents the demographic turnaround coincident with the oil boom and rising foreign-born share.

candidates.title: Labour Force Survey
candidates.description: Periodic household labour-force survey producing participation, employment and unemployment rates. Recent rounds show improving indicators but large gender gaps.
candidates.notes: Core labour-market product. Male participation and employment substantially exceed female rates; women’s unemployment is roughly double men’s in recent readings.

candidates.title: Bank of Guyana — statistical publications
candidates.description: Central-bank statistical output covering monetary aggregates, external accounts, inflation and related macroeconomic series.
candidates.notes: Monetary and external statistical authority. Complements BoS on prices, balance of payments and financial-sector indicators.

candidates.title: Natural Resource Fund (NRF)
candidates.publisher: Government of Guyana / Ministry of Finance
candidates.description: Sovereign wealth fund that receives and manages oil revenues under the Natural Resource Fund Act. Central fiscal institution of the oil era; balance reached multi-billion USD levels; withdrawal rules amended to accelerate public investment.
candidates.notes: Core fiscal-governance node of the oil boom. Continuously cited in budget, sustainability and intergenerational-equity analysis. Withdrawals now finance a large share of public investment and current spending.

candidates.title: Oil production (Stabroek / Liza and subsequent FPSOs)
candidates.description: Offshore crude-oil production from the Stabroek Block and subsequent developments. Production has risen from zero (pre-2019) to the high-hundreds of thousands of barrels per day, driving extreme GDP growth.
candidates.notes: Transformative production node. Output growth is the direct driver of the multi-year double-digit real GDP expansion and of NRF inflows. Continuously cited as the structural break in Guyana’s economic history.

candidates.title: Production Sharing Agreement — ExxonMobil consortium
candidates.publisher: Government of Guyana / ExxonMobil / Hess / CNOOC
candidates.description: Production-sharing agreement governing the Stabroek Block and related developments. Defines royalty (2% on gross production) and profit-oil split that feed the Natural Resource Fund.
candidates.notes: Foundational commercial and fiscal contract. Continuously cited as the legal and fiscal framework that converts physical production into government revenue.

candidates.title: National Accounts / GDP
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
candidates.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production and expenditure. Extreme oil-driven growth has lifted nominal GDP into the mid-to-high tens of billions of USD and per-capita GDP into upper-middle / near high-income territory on paper.
candidates.notes: Core macroeconomic product. Growth rates in the mid-to-high teens (and higher in peak years) are almost entirely oil-driven; non-oil GDP grows more moderately and is itself partly stimulated by oil-financed public spending.

candidates.title: Georgetown / Region Four (Demerara-Mahaica)
candidates.description: Capital city and the most populous administrative region. Primary urban and commercial domain; absorbs a large share of construction and service activity linked to the oil boom.
candidates.notes: Lived urban core of the transformation. Census and construction indicators show rapid housing and building growth concentrated here.

candidates.title: Poverty measurement (historical and residual)
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / World Bank / independent
candidates.description: Poverty headcount and related indicators. Pre-oil poverty was among the highest in South America; recent official poverty series are sparse, limiting assessment of how the boom has translated into broad-based welfare gains.
candidates.notes: Critical social-gap node. Pre-oil poverty headcount was very high (~40%+ in older readings). Lack of recent comprehensive poverty data is a recognised constraint on evaluating the inclusiveness of the oil-driven expansion.

proposed_edges.basis: Production volumes and fiscal take are governed by the Production Sharing Agreement.
NRF inflows are the fiscal expression of the royalty and profit-oil terms of the PSA.
Oil value-added dominates recent GDP growth.
NRF withdrawals finance public spending that feeds into non-oil GDP.
The Labour Force Survey is a core product of the Bureau of Statistics.
The census is conducted by the Bureau of Statistics.
Region Four / Georgetown is the largest geographic domain in the census.
